article.title: Why a Deadline Should Include a Time, Not Just a Day
article.why: Make the expected delivery moment explicit so teams can coordinate priorities without deadline ambiguity.
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

sources.label: Background: project scheduling and communication practice

paragraphs.en:
A deadline such as ‘Monday’ looks clear, but people can understand it in different ways. One person may think the work is due before Monday begins. Another may think it is fine to send it by the end of Monday. A third person may expect it before a Monday morning meeting. The date is the same, but the practical deadline is different.

This small ambiguity can create unnecessary stress. Imagine that your manager asks for a chart ‘by Friday.’ You plan to finish it at 4 p.m. on Friday, but the manager needs it for a 10 a.m. client meeting. Neither person intended to cause a problem. The missing information was simply the time.

A better habit is to include both the day and the time. For example: ‘I will send the draft by Friday at 3 p.m.’ If a meeting is the real reason for the deadline, you can make that visible too: ‘Please send the numbers by 9 a.m. Monday so I can use them in the 10 a.m. meeting.’

Time zones matter as well. A deadline of 5 p.m. can still be unclear when people work in different countries. Writing ‘5 p.m. JST’ or ‘9 a.m. London time’ removes another source of confusion.

You do not need to make every message formal. For small internal tasks, a short confirmation is enough: ‘Just to confirm, is Monday noon okay?’ The purpose is not to add bureaucracy. It is to make the expected delivery moment visible.

Clear deadlines also help with prioritization. When two tasks are both labeled ‘Friday,’ they appear equally urgent. If one is due at 10 a.m. and the other at 5 p.m., the order becomes easier to decide. A precise deadline is therefore not only a scheduling detail. It helps people coordinate work, set priorities, and avoid last-minute surprises.
paragraphs.zh: 只寫星期幾的 deadline 看似明確，實際上可能有人理解為當天開始前、當天下班前，或某場會議前。把日期、時間與必要時的時區一起寫出來，可以消除這種隱性歧義。精確 deadline 不只是排程細節，也能幫助團隊判斷優先順序。
paragraphs.ja: 曜日だけの締切は明確に見えても、『その日の開始前』『終業まで』『午前会議まで』など解釈が分かれます。日付と時刻、必要ならタイムゾーンまで明示すると、認識ずれを防げます。正確な締切はスケジュール管理だけでなく、優先順位付けにも役立ちます。

vocabulary.usage: Include a time in the deadline.
Clear deadlines help people coordinate work.
Two Friday tasks may not be equally urgent.
State the time zone for international teams.

phrases.term: Just to confirm, is Monday noon okay?
phrases.explanation: 簡短確認具體截止時刻。
phrases.example: Just to confirm, is Monday noon okay for the first draft?

grammar.title: by + time
grammar.body: by 表示最晚不超過某時刻，例如 by Friday at 3 p.m.

business.term: I’ll send the draft by Friday at 3 p.m. JST.
business.explanation: 同時明示日期、時間與時區。
business.example: I’ll send the draft by Friday at 3 p.m. JST.

business.term: Do you need this before the meeting?
business.explanation: 確認真正的業務 deadline 是否由會議決定。
business.example: Do you need this before the 10 a.m. meeting?

quiz.question: Why can ‘by Monday’ be ambiguous?
quiz.answer: People may interpret it as before Monday, sometime on Monday, or before a Monday event.
